## How to use this deck {.smaller}

This deck is a pattern reference, not workshop content. Each slide shows one
idiom used across our decks — copy the source, keep the class names.

- Shared options live in `_metadata.yml`; your deck YAML stays minimal
- Shared theme: `custom.scss`; slide classes: `.section-divider`, `.question-slide`, `.formula-box`
- Shared figure style: `source(here::here("_common.R"))` in a hidden setup
  chunk → use `wk_colors` and `theme_workshop()` in every plot
- Render your own deck while iterating: `quarto render slides/0X_yourdeck.qmd`
- Before handing off: run `quarto render` at the repo root once and commit the
  updated `_freeze/` folder — then nobody else re-executes your chunks

::: {.notes}
Speaker notes go in a `.notes` div — press `s` in the browser for speaker view.
:::

## Shared deck skeleton {.smaller}

Every segment follows the same section order, so attendees see the identical
workflow three times:

1. **Model intuition** — what process does the model describe?
2. **See the data** — the raw dataset, before any model
3. **Specify** — the bmm formula and model object
4. **Fit** — load the cached fit (never fit live)
5. **Evaluate** — posterior summaries, plots, hypothesis tests
6. **Extension** — richer data or model, *same workflow*
7. **Take-home** — notebook, readings, segue to the next part

Timing rule: the schedule has **no buffer**, so the *Extension* section is
your designated flex material — plan your talk so it can be cut live without
breaking the storyline if the session runs long.

## Workflow markers {.smaller}
[[specify]{.on} · fit · evaluate]{.track}

Every slide of the three bmm steps carries this **track** above its title:
the active step in blue, the others grey. It replaces a "Specify:" prefix in
the title. One line right after the heading, nothing else to set up:

```markdown
## Choose the model {.smaller}
[[specify]{.on} · fit · evaluate]{.track}

## Load the cached fit {.smaller}
[specify · [fit]{.on} · evaluate]{.track}

## Testing differences is one line {.smaller}
[specify · fit · [evaluate]{.on}]{.track}

## Ratings: more criteria, same axis {.smaller}
[[specify]{.on} · [fit]{.on} · [evaluate]{.on}]{.track}
```

- Any number of steps can be `.on`: an *Extension* slide that repeats the
  whole workflow lights all three
- On a `{.section-divider}` or `{.question-slide}` the track turns white
  automatically
- Slides outside the three steps (intuition, data, take-home) carry no track
- Styling lives in `custom.scss` under "Workflow track"; do not copy it into
  your deck

```{r}
#| echo: false

library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1)
ggplot(data.frame(x = rnorm(500)), aes(x)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = wk_colors[["blue"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = wk_colors[["orange"]], linewidth = 1) +
  theme_workshop()
```

## Code with line stepping

Use `code-line-numbers` to walk the audience through a call — each `|` group
highlights on click:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-2|4-5|7"
library(bmm)
library(here)

model <- sdt_yn(response = "n_old", stimulus = "is_old",
                n_trials = "n_trials")

fit <- bmm(bmf(d ~ 1 + (1 | id), criterion ~ 1 + (1 | id)),
           data = dat, model = model, cores = 4)
```

Illustrative syntax only (`eval: false`) — real fits are cached, see next slide.

## Loading a cached fit {.smaller}

The load-bearing pattern: **never fit live**. Fit once locally, `saveRDS()`
into `models/`, then load the cached object on the slide with a plain
`readRDS()` — no `file.exists()` guard (a guard fails *silently* and the
next chunk errors confusingly; a plain `readRDS()` fails loudly, at render
time, where you can fix it):

```{r}
#| eval: false
fit <- readRDS(here::here("models", "sdt_yn.rds"))
summary(fit)
```

(`eval: false` here only because the template ships no fit — in your deck
this chunk executes at render time.)

::: {.notes}
Workflow: fit in your examples/ notebook or a scratch script, saveRDS() to
models/ under the name contracted in models/README.md, record the bmm/brms
versions in that README's table, and commit the .rds together with your
deck and _freeze/ update. Fits must be made with CRAN versions of bmm/brms
(bmm >= 1.4.1, which carries the SDT models).
:::

## Posterior visualization

With a cached fit loaded, plot posteriors with `tidybayes` / `bayesplot`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(tidybayes)
fit |>
  gather_draws(b_d_Intercept, b_criterion_Intercept) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = .value, y = .variable)) +
  stat_halfeye()
```

(Chunk shown with `eval: false` here because the template ships no fit —
in your deck, drop that option so the plot renders from your cached model.)

## Closed-form demo figure {.smaller}

Everything on the slides is computed **at render time** — no code runs in
the browser and no network is needed at the venue. For a closed-form
"what if" (a parameter sweep, a criterion shift), show a few representative
values side by side instead of a live slider:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-alt: "ROC curves for sensitivities d-prime = 0.5, 1.5, and 2.5, with the chance diagonal as a dashed line."
far <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 200)
plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), asp = 1,
     xlab = "False-alarm rate", ylab = "Hit rate", main = "ROC curves")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = wk_colors[["grey"]])
cols <- c(wk_colors[["grey"]], wk_colors[["blue"]], wk_colors[["orange"]])
ds <- c(0.5, 1.5, 2.5)
for (i in seq_along(ds)) lines(far, pnorm(qnorm(far) + ds[i]), lwd = 3, col = cols[i])
legend("bottomright", legend = sprintf("d' = %.1f", ds), col = cols, lwd = 3, bty = "n")
```

::: {.notes}
Want to *run* something in front of the audience? Do it in the IDE from the
segment's `examples/` notebook (load the cached fit, evaluate) — the slide
carries the same output as insurance.
:::

## Formulas

Wrap display equations in a `.formula-box` for emphasis:

::: {.formula-box}
$$d' = z(\text{HR}) - z(\text{FAR}) \qquad c = -\tfrac{1}{2}\left[z(\text{HR}) + z(\text{FAR})\right]$$
:::

Inline math works as usual: the criterion $c$ shifts the response bias.

## What would you conclude? {.question-slide}

Use a `{.question-slide}` to pose a prompt to the audience before revealing
the answer on the next slide.
